notes: Group A results. SWE, KEN, PAK, BGD, AGO each yielded a private financial employer and are filed. COL (Banco de la Republica): read the bank's own biography page for board member Bibiana Taboada in full; every employer listed is public or multilateral (IDB 2006-2018, World Bank 2008, Department for Social Prosperity 2018-2020, Universidad de los Andes), no private firm at all, so nothing to file. ZMB (Bank of Zambia): the Access Bank Zambia board page returned only navigation, no biography. A MarketScreener-hosted Investrust Bank Plc announcement (16 April 2015) does state that Dr Richard K. E. Chembe, who held senior management positions at the Bank of Zambia and at the IMF, would become Investrust's managing director effective 1 May 2015, subject to Bank of Zambia approval. NOT FILED because no source opened states Investrust's ownership, and a follow-up search surfaced ZCCM-IH (the Zambian state mining investment holding company) in connection with Investrust, so private ownership cannot be confirmed. HAND CHECK: https://ca.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/INVESTRUST-BANK-PLC-8601485/news/Investrust-Bank-PLC-Announces-Directorate-Changes-38411697 plus any source stating Investrust's shareholder structure in 2015. MNG (Mongolia): read the full executive management list of Golomt Bank, 21 biographies with dated careers; not one mentions the Bank of Mongolia or Mongolbank, the only other institutions named being Mongol Post Bank, Transport and Development Bank and non-bank financial entities. The Mongolbank page reached (mongolbank.mn/en/p/6000) turned out to be the Statistics and Research landing page and carries no names or biographies, though it links to Board of Directors, Supervisory Board and Former Governors pages that were not reached. MOZ (Mozambique): read Millennium bim's own Executive Committee page, seven members with dated careers from 1989 onward; all are BCP-group careers in Portugal, Poland, Romania, Greece, Turkey and Switzerland, plus Absa, Nedbank and Standard Bank in Mozambique, and no biography mentions the Banco de Mocambique. Nothing to file. SLE (Sierra Leone): the Bank of Sierra Leone's own Board of Directors page lists nine members with names, titles and appointment dates only (Governor Ibrahim Stevens 16 November 2023, two deputy governors, six other directors) and carries no career histories, previous employers or years at all. Confirmed blank on that page; bsl.gov.sl/Management.html was not reached. KOR (South Korea): an Asiae report says Jeong Gyu-il joined the Bank of Korea in 1987 and rose to Deputy Governor, and that Seoul Foreign Exchange Brokerage appointed him CEO and President at an extraordinary shareholders' meeting. NOT FILED because the article gives no year for the appointment and says nothing about who owns Seoul Foreign Exchange Brokerage, which is understood to be held by a consortium of banks. HAND CHECK: https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2021070215182015950 plus a source on Seoul Foreign Exchange Brokerage's shareholders. BLZ (Belize): the Central Bank of Belize governance page describes the offices only, quoting the 1982 Act on a Governor and two Deputy Governors and on the Board as policy-making body, and names nobody; its Board of Directors, Office of the Governor and Past Governors sub-pages were not returned by search so were not fetched. HAND CHECK: https://www.centralbank.org.bz/about-the-bank/governance and its Board of Directors sub-page. Group B and other results. ARM filed (Ameriabank's own investor page, strongest record of the round, two directions in one source). SYC filed as a private non-financial move. URY filed twice, both found by searching the hiring firm rather than the bank. MKD (North Macedonia): the National Bank publishes individual CV pages for Vice Governor Fadil Bajrami and for Ana Mitreska and Emilija Nacevska, but the fetch of https://www.nbrm.mk:443/fadil-bajrami-biografija-en.nspx failed at the site with a client error and nothing was retrieved. HAND CHECK: https://www.nbrm.mk/fadil-bajrami-biografija-en.nspx and the sibling CV pages ana-mitreska-biografija-en.nspx and emilija-nacevska-biografija-en.nspx. HND (Honduras): the El Heraldo profile of Reina Irene Mejia gives a full private-finance career (about 25 years at Citibank Honduras, general director and head of Corporate and Investment Banking from 2013, boards of Citicredito, Citi-Inmobiliaria, Banco de Honduras and Grupo Financiero Citibank Costa Rica, IDB executive vice-president from December 2020 and interim president September-December 2022, Citi Private Bank director for Central America and the Caribbean from September 2024) but mentions no role at the Banco Central de Honduras at all, so there is no central bank leg and nothing to file. Not reached this round, no calls spent: ARM is done, but BOL DOM ECU GMB GUY NIC remain untried, as do KHM LAO MMR BRN TON. Also no AIA/Nordea-style hiring-firm sweep was run for ZMB, MNG, MOZ, SLE or BLZ beyond what is described above.

records.people: Anna Breman (Deputy Governor, later First Deputy Governor)
records.move: from Senior Economist (2013-2015) and Group Chief Economist (2015-2019) at Swedbank to Deputy Governor of Sveriges Riksbank (2019-2022), then First Deputy Governor from 2022
records.summary: The Riksbank's own CV for Anna Breman lists her employment as Senior Economist at Swedbank 2013-2015 and Group Chief Economist at Swedbank 2015-2019, then Deputy Governor of Sveriges Riksbank 2019-2022 and First Deputy Governor from 2022; Swedbank is a privately owned commercial bank listed on the Stockholm exchange, not a state body, so the outside employer is a private firm and it is in finance.

records.move: from director of Standard Chartered Bank, non-executive director of Ecobank and board member of PricewaterhouseCoopers to Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Kenya
records.summary: A Kenya Yearbook government sector profile states that Sheila M'mbijjewe was appointed Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Kenya by the President in June 2015 and served nine years on its Monetary Policy Committee, and that she had served as a director of Standard Chartered Bank, a non-executive director of Ecobank and a board member of PricewaterhouseCoopers and Stagecoach International; the page does not state dates for those roles or characterise their ownership, but Standard Chartered and Ecobank are privately owned commercial banks and PwC a private professional firm, so the outside employers are private and in finance.

records.move: from Bank of America (1976-1991), Vice President at Merrill Lynch & Co. (1992-2001) and non-executive director of United National Bank Ltd UK (2000-2006), after training at JPMorgan Chase (1973-1975), to Deputy Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan (appointed 29 March 2007) ; and on to Acting Governor (June-September 2010, again July 2011) and Governor (appointed 19 October 2011)
records.summary: The State Bank of Pakistan's own ex-governor profile for Yaseen Anwar gives a dated private-finance career before the central bank: trained at JPMorgan Chase in New York 1973-1975, about fifteen years at Bank of America 1976-1991 including Vice President and Section Head of the Global Export Finance Group, Vice President at Merrill Lynch & Co. in New York and London 1992-2001, and non-executive director of United National Bank Ltd UK 2000-2006, after which he was appointed SBP Deputy Governor on 29 March 2007 and Governor on 19 October 2011; Bank of America, Merrill Lynch and JPMorgan Chase are privately owned financial firms, so the whole outside side of this career is private finance.
records.source_title: Profile of Ex-Governor Yaseen Anwar, State Bank of Pakistan

records.move: from Deputy Governor of Bangladesh Bank (appointed February 2024 on a three-year contract, forced to resign August 2024) to Chairman of Islami Bank Bangladesh PLC (24 May 2026)
records.summary: United News of Bangladesh reports that Md. Khurshid Alam joined Bangladesh Bank as an Assistant Director in 1988, worked in banking regulation, bank inspection and SME and special programmes, was appointed Deputy Governor in February 2024 on a three-year contract and was forced to resign in August 2024 after the political transition, and was appointed Chairman of Islami Bank Bangladesh PLC on 24 May 2026; the article calls Islami Bank a private sector bank, so the outside employer is a private firm and it is in finance.
records.source_title: Former deputy governor Khurshid Alam appointed Islami Bank chairman (UNB)

records.move: from Governor of the Banco Nacional de Angola to member of the board of directors of Banco Angolano de Investimentos (BAI), elected 18 August 2015 and taking office 1 September 2015, having held those duties at BAI before
records.summary: VerAngola reports that Jose de Lima Massano, a former governor of the Banco Nacional de Angola, was elected to the board of directors of Banco Angolano de Investimentos by its general assembly on 18 August 2015, was expected to be elected president of its executive commission, had held those duties at BAI before, and was due to take office on 1 September 2015; the article itself calls BAI only an Angolan banking financial institution, but BAI's own corporate page states it was founded on 14 November 1996 as the first private bank with national capital established in Angola, so the outside employer is a private firm and it is in finance.
records.source_title: Jose de Lima Massano, ex-governador do BNA, de regresso a administracao do BAI (VerAngola)

records.people: Tigran Davtyan (several managerial roles, Central Bank of Armenia)
records.move: from director of a boutique investment company (1991, firm not named) to several managerial roles at the Central Bank of Armenia (1994-1998) ; and from the central bank onward to Deputy CEO and Head of Financial Markets at Converse Bank (2008-2009), CEO and Chairman of the Management Board of Converse Bank (2009-2016), CEO and Chairman of the Management Board of Inecobank (2018-2019) and Independent Non-Executive Director of Ameriabank (from July 2020)
records.summary: Ameriabank's own investor-relations biography of its board member Tigran Davtyan gives a dated career running both ways: director of a boutique investment company in 1991, several managerial roles at the Central Bank of Armenia 1994-1998, adviser to the Prime Minister 1998-1999, chairman of the Central Depository of Armenia 1999-2002, USAID programme roles, then Deputy CEO and Head of Financial Markets at Converse Bank 2008-2009, CEO and Chairman of the Management Board of Converse Bank 2009-2016, Director of the Financial Policy Department of the Eurasian Economic Commission 2016-2018, CEO and Chairman of the Management Board of Inecobank 2018-2019 and Independent Non-Executive Director of Ameriabank from July 2020; Converse Bank, Inecobank and Ameriabank are commercial banks and Ameriabank's own page gives its legal form as a closed joint-stock company, a privately held form rather than a state body, so the outside side of this career is private finance.
records.source_title: Tigran Davtyan, Board of Directors, Ameriabank

records.people: Martin Inthamoussu (adviser to the Board, then Vice-President)
records.move: from the Banco Central del Uruguay, where he was adviser to the Board from 2020 to 2025 and Vice-President from August 2024 to April 2025, to the Uruguayan wealth management firm Nobilis, announced October 2026
records.summary: RankiaPro reports that Martin Inthamoussu was part of the Banco Central del Uruguay between 2020 and 2025, serving as adviser to its Board and, in his final stage, as Vice-President from August 2024 to April 2025, and that he has joined the Uruguayan wealth management firm Nobilis to strengthen compliance, risk management and processes, in an announcement published in October 2026; the article does not use the word private, but Nobilis is a wealth management firm with no stated state ownership, so the outside employer is a private firm and it is in finance.
records.source_title: La firma uruguaya de gestion patrimonial Nobilis incorporo a un exvicepresidente del Banco Central (RankiaPro)

records.move: from President of the Banco Central del Uruguay (2020-2024) to General Manager of the Bolsa Electronica de Valores (Bevsa), named by its board on 20 August 2025
records.summary: RankiaPro reports that Diego Labat, president of the Banco Central del Uruguay from 2020 to 2024, was named General Manager of the Bolsa Electronica de Valores (Bevsa) by its board on 20 August 2025, replacing Eduardo Barbieri after 25 years in the post; the employer is in finance, but the article states that Bevsa was founded in January 1993 by 26 financial institutions operating in Uruguay, both public and private, so its ownership is mixed rather than plainly private and this record should be treated as a weaker private-finance case than the others.
records.source_title: En Uruguay, la Bolsa Electronica de Valores tiene a expresidente del Banco Central como nuevo gerente general (RankiaPro)

records.people: James Jean (Board Director; previously Head of the Financial Inclusion and Market Conduct Division)
records.move: from about thirteen years at the Central Bank of Seychelles (2008-2021, last post Head of the Financial Inclusion and Market Conduct Division) out to managing two private businesses, one in agriculture and one in manufacturing, and back to the Central Bank of Seychelles as a board director from 1 June 2023
records.summary: Seychelles Nation reports that James Jean worked at the Central Bank of Seychelles for about thirteen years from 2008 to 2021 in banking supervision and payment systems oversight, his last post being Head of the Financial Inclusion and Market Conduct Division, that for roughly the two years before his appointment he managed two businesses of his own, one in agriculture and one in manufacturing, which the article calls private sector experience without naming them, and that he then joined the bank's board of directors on a six-year appointment effective 1 June 2023; the outside employers are private companies outside finance, so this is logged rather than counted as a private finance move.
records.source_title: CBS board gets additional new member (Seychelles Nation)
